title: Sidecar-assisted offline upgrade acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating Redwood Private in VPC / air-gapped environments require a deterministic, zero-egress upgrade path. Existing upgrade flows assume direct outbound access for artifact pulls or controller callbacks. For highly restricted networks we propose a sidecar-assisted offline upgrade model: a lightweight sidecar running adjacent to the operator that coordinates artifact syncs from customer-approved mirrors, performs integrity checks, and orchestrates local handoff to the operator for a final in-cluster activation.

Scope: This ticket captures product-level requirements and acceptance criteria for the sidecar-assisted offline upgrade flow. It covers networking constraints (zero or tightly controlled egress), upgrade orchestration semantics (canary, staged, atomic activation), artifact validation (catalog signatures, checksums), operational observability, and rollback/runbook requirements. Implementation details live in linked PRD and engineering EPICs.

Out of scope: UI polish in Console, broader Dedicated autoscaling changes, and unrelated KMS provider integrations beyond the minimal rotation contract required for offline upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Zero-egress compatibility: The sidecar + operator upgrade flow can complete a full minor-version image and operator binary upgrade without requiring outbound connections, assuming customer provides a reachable mirror containing signed artifacts and a signed catalog. Verification steps must not attempt DNS or HTTP calls outside the VPC when in "airgap" mode.

AC-2: Signed catalog validation: The operator/sidecar verifies artifact provenance using an on-disk signed catalog (PKI signature verification). The process rejects any artifact not present in the catalog or whose signature fails verification. Test vectors include tampered manifest and missing signature scenarios.

AC-3: Checksums and atomic handoff: Artifacts are downloaded to a sidecar-managed staged location and their checksums validated. Only after successful validation does the sidecar instruct the operator to switch to the new artifact; the switch is atomic from operator perspective (either old or new manifests active).

AC-4: Canary and staged activation: The flow supports a configurable canary subset (1-5% of nodes or single NodePool) with health gating. Canary must be able to roll forward to full rollout automatically on green health signals, or roll back on failure.

AC-5: Local fallback: If the mirror is unreachable or verification fails, cluster remains on previous version and sidecar surfaces a clear failure state and remediation steps. No partial cluster upgrade is allowed without passing integrity gates.

AC-6: Operator and sidecar RBAC: Communication between operator and sidecar uses in-cluster RBAC tokens; no external keys are stored unencrypted. Acceptance requires KMS/HSM-backed key handling where customer KMS is available; otherwise documented manual rotation steps are acceptable.

AC-7: Observability and audit trail: Upgrade events, artifact checksums, signature verification results, and operator activation events are emitted to the local audit log and visible in the Console (when Console has connectivity). In air-gapped mode, logs must be exportable as bundles (tar.gz) for offline review.

AC-8: Runbook & rollback tested: Documented runbook for common failure modes (mirror corruption, insufficient disk on node, signature mismatch). Automated rollback must be runnable from operator CLI and revert cluster to the pre-upgrade state within defined SLA (default: 10 minutes for control-plane bounded upgrades).
AC-9: Performance guardrails: Upgrade staging must respect node disk and CPU limits; sidecar will not start downloads if free disk < configurable threshold (default 2x artifact size).

AC-10: Security gates: Any deployment marked 'airgap-strict' requires security review before activation. Acceptance includes completed security checklist and one penetration-oriented test vector (artifact tampering) verified by security team.

rollback_plan: If staged activation fails post-catalog-verify, the sidecar marks the activation as failed and leaves the operator on the previous image. Operator exposes an escape hatch: 'redwood operator rollback --to-revision <rev>' which re-applies saved manifests and restarts pods in order. For catastrophic control-plane failure, operator falls back to saved pre-upgrade backup tarball; cluster operator must follow runbook to perform node-level restore. Ensure clear operator CLI errors and automatically upload a diagnostics bundle when possible.
test_plan: TP-1: End-to-end test in airgap lab — customer mirror populated with signed catalog. Verify full upgrade success without outbound requests (network capture to confirm).
TP-2: Tampered manifest test — alter signature in catalog, expect rejection and no activation. Verify audit log contains signature failure event.
TP-3: Mirror intermittent availability — simulate mirror flaps during canary, ensure rollback triggers and operator remains stable.
TP-4: Disk pressure test — force node disk below threshold during staging, ensure sidecar aborts download and surfaces error.
TP-5: Canary health gating — create failing service post-canary and verify automated rollback path and time-to-rollback under SLA.
operator_notes: Sidecar is intentionally minimal: download, verify, stage, trigger operator activation. No automatic artifact verification bypass allowed. Operators should have a 'dry-run' mode for on-prem validation. Provide a 'bundle export' command for offline support requests. Provide descriptive exit codes for automation integration.
